chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is a compact cosmological narrative about Matter's envy expressed through three cosmic episodes: the First Man, the Ambassador's image, and Adam. This substrate is clearly bounded — paragraphs 2-4 are pure cosmological narrative with both sides of every mapping internal to the cosmic system. The editors extended the three-fold enumeration to a fourth item (Christ and the apostles), then to Mani and his church, then to practical community warnings, then to exhortation. The editorial fatigue pattern is textbook: institutional vocabulary jumps from 0.0 to 8.30 in the second half. Teaching purity is very low (0.109), reflecting that the substrate core is small and the editorial extension substantial.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] entirety of envy is this first nature that occu[red] in the worlds of darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula: 'Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: The thesis statement — envy as the 'first nature' in 'the worlds of darkness' — is a cosmological identification with both sides internal to the cosmic system. The frame formula is standard dialogue layer wrapping.

paragraphs.core_text: In this envy that [ ... ] in it, the First Man [ ... ] its poiso[n ... ] its evil-doing. His garment[s] were [ ... ] it cut them and drew them; [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite heavy lacunae, the cosmological content is clear: Matter's envy directed at the First Man, a cosmic entity. 'His garments' are the five light elements in Manichaean cosmology (the Sons of First Man). The cutting and drawing of garments describes the cosmic capture. Both sides of the mapping are internal to the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.179⟩ It envied the first image of the Ambassador, which he displayed to it in the heights abov[e], i[n] his form that it saw. It established the seal and the image of flesh, and put the impression of t[h]at image on flesh, its very own birth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The second stage of the cosmic enumeration. The Ambassador (Third Messenger) displaying his image and Matter's reactive creation of the fleshly copy — this is standard Manichaean cosmological narrative. 'The seal and the image of flesh' describes Matter's imitation of the cosmic image. Both sides remain within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: [The th]ird time it envied Adam, the fir[st hum]an. It seized a power from him, and bore it forth from a [rib of] of Adam's [flesh].
paragraphs.temporal_note: The third stage. Adam here is a cosmic figure in the Manichaean drama, not a historical person. The seizing of power from his rib is the creation of Eve — a cosmic event in the entrapment narrative. Both sides internal to the cosmic system. Note 'the first human' as a cosmic title.

The 'fourth time' mimics the substrate enumeration pattern but the content shifts decisively: 'the blessed Christ who is the father of all the apostles' (institutional title), 'the wood of the cross' (historical event), 'fathers of righteousness' and 'congregations' (institutional terms). One side of the mapping now reaches into the historical/religious world. The three-fold cosmic enumeration (First Man, Ambassador, Adam) was likely the complete substrate teaching; this fourth item is an editorial extension into salvation history.

Editorial seam correctly flagged. 'Furthermore' bridges from the teaching enumeration to Mani's first-person institutional narrative. Dense institutional vocabulary: 'my church', 'my catechumens', 'this last generation', 'great person or a disciple, a man or a woman, a male catechumen or a female catechumen.' The entire paragraph is one editorial act extending the cosmic teaching to the Manichaean community's present.

Describes how sin/envy operates in the contemporary community: 'false reports and lying accusations', 'the teacher and the righteous elect person', 'He who preaches.' The cosmic force (Matter/Sin) is mapped onto specific community dynamics — one side of the mapping reaches into the editor's world. 'Teacher', 'elect person' are institutional roles.

The cosmological terms 'the desire of Matter, the thought of death' and 'the envy of its wickedness' and 'the entire kindred of life' are present but deployed within an editorial summary. 'They fall from the faith' describes community members. 'From the very beginning until my time, from me too to my church' explicitly anchors to Mani's institutional present. The 'This is' formula here functions as editorial summary, not substrate description.

Classic devotional closure: 'Therefore, it is appropriate for the wise person that he be steadfast and strong.' Moral application addressed to the audience. 'Stand firm in God', 'stay with his hope and his faith', 'he overcomes' — all standard exhortation vocabulary. The 'Therefore' signals the editorial pivot from teaching to application.
